review_notes: I read the whole target file and the relevant part of FiniteDiagramIndDual.lean (continuousEquiv, _id, _comp, _apply_class). I only checked this one rubric. Many theorems here (indDualRealizationMap_apply_class, indDualRealizationComparison_apply_class, indDualRealizationComparison_inv_apply_class) are thin wrappers around finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousEquiv_apply_class, so I did not report them. The map_comp, naturality and inv_eq_continuousEquiv proofs share a short "congr 1; simp [assoc]" step around _comp. I judged that too short to count. The one finding is the hom_inv_id/inv_hom_id pair in indDualRealizationComparison. I have not compiled the proposed lemma, so the argument-order details are uncertain.

findings.problem: The two isomorphism laws repeat the same argument. Each one rewrites a composite of two continuous-equiv images as the image of the composite via finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousEquiv_comp. Each then cancels the presentation iso with Iso.hom_inv_id or Iso.inv_hom_id. Finally each closes with finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousEquiv_id. The first is a calc and the second is a simpa, and each restates a very large `change` goal full of repeated `indDualPresentationDiagram (finiteDiagramIndDual X)` / `indDualPresentationCone ...` / `Profinite.limitConeIsLimit _` terms. The same fact, that the continuous equivalence sends an isomorphism of finite-diagram ind-objects to an isomorphism of the limits, is therefore proved twice for one specific iso. It is not stated once in general form.
findings.proposed_change: Add a general lemma or definition next to finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousEquiv_comp (in FiniteDiagramIndDual.lean or earlier in this file). For X : I ⥤ Skeleton, Y : J ⥤ Skeleton, limit cones (c,hc), (d,hd), and e : finiteDiagramIndDual X ≅ finiteDiagramIndDual Y, define `finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousIso X Y c hc d hd e : c.pt ≅ d.pt`. Its hom is `continuousEquiv X Y c hc d hd e.hom` and its inv is `continuousEquiv Y X d hd c hc e.inv`. Prove hom_inv_id once with `(finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousEquiv_comp ..).symm`, then `e.hom_inv_id`, then `_id`. Prove inv_hom_id the same way, now with generic X and Y so the goals are short. Then `indDualRealizationComparison X c hc` becomes `finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousIso _ X _ (Profinite.limitConeIsLimit _) c hc (indDualPresentationIso (finiteDiagramIndDual X))`. The two 25-line proofs with their long `change` blocks disappear. The existing uses of the comparison's hom and inv, such as indDualRealizationComparison_apply_class and _inv_apply_class, stay valid by `rfl`/unfolding. The lemma needs no extra hypotheses beyond those already imposed on I, J, K (SmallCategory and IsCofiltered), so imports are unchanged. The same iso could also serve indDualRealizationComparisonOfIso_inv_eq_continuousEquiv.
findings.benefit: The invertibility argument is stated once in generic form, so readers see the real content (functoriality of continuousEquiv on isos) without the restated goals. Maintenance is easier: a change in the shape of finiteDiagramIndDualContinuousEquiv_comp or _id is fixed in one place rather than in two near-copy proofs. The generic iso is also reusable for other presentation changes.
